scheme_name: PMMSY: Construction of Ice Plant/Storage of Minimum 10 Tonne Capacity - Gujarat
description:
The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) is a flagship scheme launched by the Government of India on September 10, 2020. 

This scheme aims to bring about a significant transformation in the fisheries sector. 

The PMMSY is designed to enhance fish production and productivity in India. 

The scheme is part of the broader initiative to promote sustainable and responsible fishing practices. 

The PMMSY is implemented in various states, including Gujarat. 

In Gujarat, one of the key components of PMMSY is the construction of ice plants and storage facilities. 

These facilities must have a minimum capacity of 10 tonnes. 

The objective of this initiative is to reduce post-harvest losses in the fisheries sector. 

Post-harvest losses in fish can be as high as 20 to 30 percent due to inadequate storage and handling facilities. 

The establishment of ice plants is crucial for maintaining the quality and freshness of fish. 

The scheme aims to provide financial assistance to fishers and fish farmers. 

The financial assistance is aimed at promoting the construction of ice plants and cold storage facilities. 

The assistance provided under this scheme can go up to 60 percent of the total project cost. 

For the construction of ice plants, the maximum grant amount can reach ₹50 lakh. 

This means that if the total project cost is ₹83.33 lakh, the beneficiary can receive ₹50 lakh as a subsidy. 

The remaining amount must be borne by the beneficiaries themselves. 

The beneficiaries can be individuals, cooperatives, or self-help groups involved in the fisheries sector. 

The eligibility criteria for this scheme are specific. 

Applicants must be engaged in fish production or aquaculture activities. 

They must also demonstrate a commitment to sustainable fishing practices. 

There is no specific age limit for applicants under this scheme. 

However, they must possess the necessary skills and knowledge related to fish handling and storage. 

The application process for the PMMSY scheme is straightforward. 

Interested beneficiaries must submit their applications to the respective state fisheries department. 

The application must include a detailed project report. 

This report should outline the proposed construction of the ice plant or storage facility. 

Additionally, applicants must provide proof of their engagement in the fisheries sector. 

Documents required include identity proof, address proof, and bank account details. 

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the state fisheries department. 

If approved, the project will be sanctioned, and the financial assistance will be disbursed. 

The disbursement of funds is typically done in installments. 

The first installment is released upon project approval. 

Subsequent installments are released based on the progress of the construction. 

The timeline for project completion is generally set at 12 months from the date of approval. 

The implementing authority for this scheme in Gujarat is the Department of Fisheries. 

This department operates under the Government of Gujarat. 

They are responsible for monitoring the implementation and progress of the PMMSY. 

The contact details for the Department of Fisheries in Gujarat can be found on their official website. 

The PMMSY also emphasizes the importance of skill development. 

Training programs are organized to enhance the skills of fishers and fish farmers. 

These programs focus on modern fishing techniques and sustainable practices. 

The scheme also aims to promote the use of technology in the fisheries sector. 

This includes the adoption of modern storage and handling equipment. 

The PMMSY is expected to create employment opportunities in the fisheries sector. 

It is estimated that the scheme will generate around 15 lakh direct and indirect jobs. 

The overall investment under PMMSY is projected to be around ₹20,050 crore. 

This investment is aimed at increasing fish production to 220 lakh tonnes by 2024-25. 

The scheme also aims to increase the contribution of the fisheries sector to the Gross Domestic Product (GDP). 

Currently, the fisheries sector contributes approximately 1.24 percent to the national GDP. 

The PMMSY is aligned with the vision of doubling farmers' income by 2022. 

The scheme also supports the Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative. 

This initiative aims to make India self-reliant in various sectors, including fisheries. 

The PMMSY is not only focused on production but also on value addition. 

The establishment of ice plants and storage facilities will facilitate value addition in fish products. 

This will help in enhancing the income of fishers and fish farmers. 

The scheme also promotes the establishment of fish markets and processing units. 

These markets will provide better prices for fishers and improve their livelihoods. 

The PMMSY is a comprehensive scheme that addresses various challenges in the fisheries sector. 

It aims to create a sustainable and profitable fisheries ecosystem in India. 

The scheme is expected to significantly boost the fisheries sector in Gujarat. 

It will enhance the quality of fish products and reduce wastage. 

The construction of ice plants and storage facilities is a crucial step towards achieving these goals. 

The PMMSY is a testament to the Government of India's commitment to the fisheries sector. 

It reflects the importance of sustainable practices in ensuring food security and economic growth. 

The scheme is a vital initiative for the development of the fisheries sector in Gujarat and across India. 

The PMMSY is a significant opportunity for stakeholders in the fisheries sector to improve their operations. 

By participating in this scheme, beneficiaries can contribute to the overall growth of the fisheries industry. 

The PMMSY is a forward-looking initiative that aims to transform the fisheries landscape in India. 

It is essential for stakeholders to stay informed about the scheme and its benefits. 

This knowledge will enable them to take full advantage of the opportunities presented by the PMMSY.
